cards.q: What is a Wireless LAN Controller (WLC)?
cards.a: The WLC is the brain of a centralized WLAN: it configures APs, runs RRM, handles client authentication and roaming, and anchors the control plane via CAPWAP. APs are lite devices — the WLC pushes config and management/control traffic flows through it.

cards.q: What functions does a WLC perform?
cards.a: It pushes AP config profiles, runs RRM for channels/power, handles authentication (RADIUS/802.1X), manages client roaming handoff, and provides monitoring. Central admin means one place to configure the whole AP fleet.

cards.q: Where do the control, management, and data planes live in a centralized WLAN?
cards.a: Control (CAPWAP control) and management live on the WLC; data goes from AP to WLC, or stays local with FlexConnect. The split means the AP handles RF while the WLC handles policy.

cards.q: What are the WLC AP modes and their data paths?
cards.a: Local sends client data to the WLC; FlexConnect keeps data local to the AP for remote branches; Monitor only senses; Sniffer captures traffic.

cards.q: What is the AP join process to a WLC?
cards.a: The AP discovers the controller via DNS/L3, performs CAPWAP discovery, establishes the DTLS secure tunnel, and receives its config and software push.

cards.q: What are the WLC management ports used for?
cards.a: The Management port handles admin/dashboard, the AP manager port handles AP traffic, and the Service port handles guest traffic. Separate subinterfaces/VRFs keep the planes isolated.

cards.q: What WLC platform types exist and which is the modern controller?
cards.a: Appliance (9800 series), embedded (Catalyst/AIRE), virtual (vWLC), and cloud (Catalyst Center). The 9800 series is the modern IOS-XE controller.

cards.q: What commands verify WLC, AP, and WLAN status?
cards.a: show ap summary, show ap join stats summary, show wlan summary, show wireless stats, and show ap config general.

cards.q: An AP is not joining the WLC. What are the likely causes and the check?
cards.a: Likely CAPWAP or DNS problems. Check with show ap join stats summary and verify CAPWAP discovery and DNS resolution.

cards.q: No WLANs, failing auth, broken roaming, and wrong data path appear. What should you check?
cards.a: No WLANs means WLANs are not enabled (show wlan summary); auth failures point to RADIUS (show wireless stats); roaming failures point to mobility config; and wrong data path points to the AP mode (Local vs FlexConnect).

cards.q: Which plane is NOT always on the WLC?
cards.a: The data plane is not always on the WLC — in FlexConnect mode client data stays local at the AP, while control and management always remain on the WLC.

cards.q: In which WLC AP mode does client data stay local at the AP?
cards.a: FlexConnect mode keeps client data local to the AP (intended for remote branches), unlike Local mode which tunnels it to the WLC.

cards.q: Which WLC quick review facts should you remember?
cards.a: The WLC is the central brain using CAPWAP; control and management are on the WLC; data is on the WLC or FlexConnect; RRM and auth (RADIUS) run on the WLC; modes are local/flex/monitor/sniffer; the 9800 is the modern platform.
